result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_node_vitality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the vitality of a single node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24961-L25070){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_vitality(node) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node vitality](/assets/graphs/get-node-vitality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with the queried hub C outlined and its four edges dashed, as if removed. The neighbors can still reach each other around C, so the total pairwise distance only drops from 82 to 70 and the card reads vitality 12." width="100%"} Node vitality measures the impact of removing a node on graph connectivity, defined as the change in sum of all pairwise shortest path distances: vitality(v) = sum_distances(G) - sum_distances(G - v) Higher values indicate more important nodes. Only finite distances are summed: if removing the node leaves some pairs unable to reach each other, those pairs simply drop out of `sum_distances(G - v)`, so the result is always finite. This matches `closeness_vitality()`, which computes the same value for every node at once. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID (int) or label (str) to compute vitality for. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The vitality score for the node. Higher values indicate more vital nodes. Always finite, even when removing the node disconnects the graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Vitality is defined as the increase in the network's total pairwise distance caused by removing a single node: $\mathrm{vit}(v) = W(G) - W(G - v)$, where $W(G) = \sum_{u \ne w} d(u, w)$ is the Wiener index, summed over reachable pairs only. Removing a cut vertex makes some distances infinite; those pairs are left out rather than making the result infinite, so cut vertices tend to score high because many long paths disappear along with them. Because computing $W$ requires an all-pairs shortest-path pass, the cost is $O(V \cdot E)$ per node, so for many nodes it is dramatically cheaper to call `closeness_vitality()` once and read every value out of the same shared BFS pass. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 5-node path, the middle node has the highest vitality (36): removing it splits the path in two, and every long distance across the middle drops out of the total. An endpoint scores lower (20): ::: {#97881760 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(5) nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) # The middle node: removing it splits the path in two graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[2]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 36.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#918d32f3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # An endpoint graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 20.0 ``` ::: ::: The same pattern shows up in a star graph: the hub lies on every path between leaves, so it outscores any individual leaf: ::: {#ee2bd95d .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_star_graph(4) nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) # The hub graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 18.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#03ec13ec .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # A leaf graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 10.0 ``` ::: ::: Node labels work just as well as IDs: ::: {#c9a99548 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # B connects A and C, so it is the most vital node here graph.get_node_vitality("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 8.0 ``` ::: :::
